title: Revising a decision without a trial
meaning: Shared responsibility helps you revise a decision when discovering an error does not become a trial of each other.
text: Even a carefully weighed decision can meet a fact that changes the original picture. Justice in the physical position of Manipura helps you check conditions and act through a clear agreement. Justice in energy identifies the wish to preserve fairness and answer for your contribution. The Tower in emotions shows the force of shock when the calculation you relied on proves unsound. That feeling establishes nobody’s guilt. It shows how difficult the collapse of a foundation can feel when you both depended on it while choosing.

Suppose you order parts for a table, checking measurements and sharing the cost. During assembly, you discover a projection omitted from the product description. **Shared responsibility can survive an incorrect calculation.** You now need to understand the available options together, without immediately deciding who should have guessed. The difficulty remains unpleasant, while returning or adapting the parts can again become a decision based on clear conditions and participation.

The difficulty begins if restoring fairness immediately requires someone to blame. You examine earlier words, compare attentiveness and try to regain certainty by proving the other person’s mistake. The original shock then continues between you. Honesty includes acknowledging the limits of what you both knew. That recognition can restore your ability to decide when the old arrangement no longer works and no ready answer has yet appeared.
